 1               P R O C E E D I N G S

 2                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   The 

 3   Senate will come to order.

 5   rise and repeat with me the Pledge of 

 6   Allegiance.

 7                (Whereupon, the assemblage recited 

 8   the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

 9                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   We are 

10   very pleased to have with us today Lieutenant 

11   Colonel Harold E. Cline, Jr., who's with us this 

12   morning to give our invocation.  Colonel Cline 

13   is the chaplain for the United States Corps of 

14   Cadets at West Point, New York.

15                Chaplain.

16                CHAPLAIN CLINE:   Ladies and 

17   gentlemen, I invite you to pray with me if you 

18   so choose.  

19                Almighty Father, we thank You for 

20   the beauty of this day and particularly the 

21   beauty that is the State of New York.  We're 

22   grateful for her.  We're grateful for her 

23   people, their lives and their work.

24                We ask that this august body would 

25   be a blessing and ask Your wisdom and guidance 


                                                                2167

 1   as these leaders seek to serve the citizens of 

 2   the Empire State.

 3                Today we celebrate the rich 

 4   relationship that the State of New York has with 

 5   the United States Military Academy at West Point.  

 6   And the native sons and daughters of this state 

 7   who represent the United States Corps of Cadets 

 8   here today carry with them the promise of a 

 9   future that is a gift both to America at large 

10   and to New York in particular.

11                For that reason, we join today to 

12   thank You for those pioneers, both military and 

13   civilian, who paved the way to transform that 

14   formidable bend in the Hudson River into not only 

15   a fortress, but an incubator for future leaders 

16   of character.  

17                May what we do and say here today 

18   ring with truth and demonstrate our resolve to 

19   leave our citizenry the gift of a future built 

20   upon the legacy of trust, strength and freedom.  

21   Grant that we would do our duty, live with honor, 

22   and serve our country.  

23                God bless the United States Military 

24   Academy.  God bless the great State of New York.  

25   And God bless the United States of America.  


                                                                2168

 1                Amen.  

 2                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   We are 

 3   very pleased today to have with us Lieutenant 

 4   General Robert Caslen, the superintendent of the 

 5   United States Military Academy at West Point.  

 6   We'll ask him to address the Senate today.

 7                General, the floor is yours.

 8                SUPERINTENDENT CASLEN:   Thank you 

 9   very much.

10                Senator Flanagan and Senator Larkin 

11   and members of this distinguished Senate, good 

12   morning and thank you for having us here today.

13                It's an honor to address you this 

14   morning on behalf of the entire staff, faculty, 

15   and the Corps of Cadets at the United States 

16   Military Academy, and we thank you very much for 

17   this recognition.  

18                I am pleased here to be representing 

19   the Academy, along with my Command Sergeant Major 

20   David Clark; Cadet E.J. Coleman, who is our First 

21   Captain for the Corps of Cadets; and 13 cadets 

22   from across New York, representing the more than 

23   4,000 members of the Corps of Cadets, 275 of 

24   which call the Empire State home.

25                The United States Army has always 


                                                                2169

 1   had a strong presence in New York, dating back to 

 2   the American Revolution.  New York has a rich 

 3   history of military service.  Many New Yorkers 

 4   have served with valor and distinction.  Numerous 

 5   of them have made the ultimate sacrifice, and we 

 6   will never forget them.  

 7                We greatly appreciate the tremendous 

 8   support provided by the State Legislature, the 

 9   towns and communities and families that support 

10   our mission in many ways.  West Point's mission 

11   is to educate, train and inspire the Corps of 

12   Cadets so that each graduate is a commissioned 

13   leader of character committed to the values of 

14   duty, honor, country, and prepared for a career 

15   of professional excellence in service to the 

16   nation as an officer in the United States Army.

17                We could not do this without the 

18   continued support of the New York Legislature and 

19   the surrounding communities outside our gates.  

20   So it is important to me as superintendent that 

21   we work hard to be good neighbors with your 

22   communities, but that we also look for ways to 

23   continue to connect and build relationships and 

24   partner together on opportunities that will not 

25   only enhance our cadet development at West Point, 


                                                                2170

 1   but also benefit the community as well.

 2                These young men and women with me 

 3   today represent what's been referred to as the 

 4   9/11 generation, and they represent the very best 

 5   of America.  They are a generation of young men 

 6   and women that saw our nation brutally attacked 

 7   and yet they volunteered to serve, knowing full 

 8   well that when they graduated they would be sent 

 9   into harm's way.  They desire to serve something 

10   bigger than themselves, and in this case our 

11   nation.  That desire to serve echoes the actions 

12   of those who served before them.  They understand 

13   service, and they understand sacrifice.  

14                Every day we at West Point aspire to 

15   be the world's premier leader development 

16   institution, developing leaders prepared to fight 

17   and win our nation's wars.  This requires a 

18   dedicated team, many of whom are from our local 

19   communities, who are committed to creating the 

20   culture of professional excellence needed to 

21   develop leaders of character for our nation.

22                As superintendent, I am proud to 

23   lead such an amazing team of professionals.  Our 

24   core values at West Point are duty, honor and 

25   country, and I would submit that our cadets have 


                                                                2171

 1   inherited and internalized duty and country even 

 2   before they enter our gates.

 3                President Bush once said that if 

 4   anyone tells you that America's best days are 

 5   behind her, they're looking the wrong way.  I 

 6   truly believe that our nation's best days are 

 7   ahead of us because of the incredible young men 

 8   and women of this generation, who wear the cloth 

 9   of our nation and say, every day:  "Send me."  I 

10   am proud of them, and I know you are as well.

11                If you haven't been to West Point 

12   lately, or if you've never been to West Point, 

13   please come and visit with us and come to see 

14   your academy.  Talk to our staff and faculty and 

15   talk to our cadets.  I promise you they will 

16   inspire you as they inspire me every day.  

17                Thank you very much for honoring all 

18   of us here at West Point today.  

19                Go Army, beat Navy!  Thank you.  

20                (Laughter.)

21                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   Thank you, 

22   General.

23                (Standing ovation.)

 4                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

 5   Resolution Number 5155, by Senator Larkin, 

 6   memorializing Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to 

 7   proclaim May 5, 2016, as West Point Day in the 

 8   State of New York.

 9                "WHEREAS, This Legislative Body is 

10   justly proud to celebrate the establishment of 

11   the United States Military Academy at West Point 

12   and to call upon Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to 

13   proclaim May 5, 2016, as West Point Day in the 

14   State of New York; and 

15                "WHEREAS, By an act of Congress, on 

16   March 16, 1802, the United States Military 

17   Academy was established within the borders of 

18   New York State, on the banks of the Hudson River; 

19   and 

20                "WHEREAS, The Academy and its 

21   graduates are an integral part of the proud 

22   history of this state and nation; and 

23                "WHEREAS, The leadership and 

24   sacrifices of the members of the Long Gray Line 

25   have helped this country withstand countless  


                                                                2174

 1   threats to our cherished democratic way of life; 

 2   and 

 3                "WHEREAS, The alumni have excelled 

 4   not only on the battlefield but in many fields of 

 5   endeavor; and 

 6                "WHEREAS, The Academy continues to 

 7   provide our country with able and dedicated 

 8   future leaders; and 

 9                "WHEREAS, Its scenic campus is a 

10   mecca each year for thousands of visitors from 

11   across our state, continent and other countries; 

12   and 

13                "WHEREAS, The United States Military 

14   Academy is in the forefront of our state's 

15   outstanding institutions of higher learning; and 

16                "WHEREAS, Sixty-four years ago, the 

17   late James T. McNamara, then a member of the 

18   New York State Assembly, and a member of the 

19   Academy's Class of 1939, was the author of the 

20   State Legislature's first 'West Point Day' 

21   resolution; and 

22                "WHEREAS, For decades, our nation 

23   has enjoyed the legacy of freedom and the 

24   United States Military Academy at West Point has  

25   played a vitally significant role in the 


                                                                2175

 1   maintenance of peace and freedom; and 

 2                "WHEREAS, The members of this 

 3   Legislative Body are proud to commemorate this 

 4   event, marking May 5, 2016, as West Point Day in 

 5   New York State; now, therefore, be it 

 6                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

 7   Body pause in its deliberations to celebrate the 

 8   establishment of the United States Military 

 9   Academy at West Point and to memorialize Governor 

10   Andrew M. Cuomo to proclaim May 5, 2016, as 

11   West Point Day in New York State; and be it 

12   further 

13                "RESOLVED, That a copy of this  

14   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to  

15   the Honorable Andrew M. Cuomo, Governor of the 

16   State of New York."

                                                                2178

 1   my day was, thank God, I had the opportunity to 

 2   serve with men from the Long Gray Line.  And I 

 3   served 23 years with them.  And never was I 

 4   ashamed of one person that came from the 

 5   Long Gray Line.  Their leadership, their respect, 

 6   their complete contempt for those who didn't want 

 7   to make it right was something.

 8                But everything that was done was -- 

 9   the mission was first.  The troops were first.

18                Thank you, and God bless you.
